Package utilities

Interface QueueADT

All Known Implementing Classes:
MyQueue
public interface QueueADT
A Queue ADT interface used as the foundation for queue data structures in CPRG 304 at SAIT.

This interface embodies all standard queue operations — enqueue, dequeue, peek — as well as several helper methods that provide additional flexibility. A queue follows a First-In, First-Out (FIFO) ordering policy: the first element enqueued is the first one returned by a dequeue or peek operation.

Design Note – String-Specific Implementation:
This interface is intentionally designed to work with String elements only. A fully reusable, type-safe design would use Java generics (e.g., QueueADT<E>), allowing any object type to be stored in the queue. Generic programming is outside the scope of CPRG 304 and has therefore been omitted. All element parameters and return types are fixed as String throughout this interface and its implementations.

  • Method Details

    • enqueue

      void enqueue(String toAdd) throws NullPointerException
      Adds the specified String element to the end of this queue.

      After this call, the enqueued element becomes the new tail of the queue. It will be the last element returned relative to all elements currently present. null values are not permitted.

      Parameters:
      toAdd - the String element to add to the end of the queue; must not be null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if toAdd is null

    • dequeue

      String dequeue() throws EmptyQueueException
      Removes and returns the String element at the front of this queue.

      The element that has been in the queue the longest is removed first, consistent with FIFO ordering. The element directly behind the removed front becomes the new head of the queue after this call.

      Returns:
      the String element removed from the front of the queue
      Throws:
      EmptyQueueException - if the queue contains no elements

    • peek

      String peek() throws EmptyQueueException
      Returns the String element at the front of this queue without removing it.

      The state of the queue is unchanged after this call.

      Returns:
      the String element currently at the front of the queue
      Throws:
      EmptyQueueException - if the queue contains no elements

    • dequeueAll

      void dequeueAll()
      Removes all elements from this queue, leaving it empty. After this call, size() returns 0 and isEmpty() returns true.

    • isEmpty

      boolean isEmpty()
      Returns true if this queue contains no elements.
      Returns:
      true if size() is 0; false otherwise

    • contains

      boolean contains(String toFind) throws NullPointerException
      Returns true if this queue contains at least one occurrence of the specified String element.

      Equality is determined using String.equals(Object).

      Parameters:
      toFind - the String element to search for; must not be null
      Returns:
      true if the element is present; false otherwise
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if toFind is null

    • search

      int search(String toFind)
      Returns the 1-based position of the specified String element from the front of this queue.

      The front element is at position 1, the element directly behind it is at position 2, and so on. If the element appears more than once, the position of the occurrence nearest the front is returned. Equality is determined using String.equals(Object).

      Parameters:
      toFind - the String element to search for
      Returns:
      the 1-based distance from the front of the queue to the nearest occurrence of the element, or -1 if the element is not present in the queue

    • iterator

      Iterator iterator()
      Returns an Iterator that traverses the String elements of this queue in proper sequence, from front to back.
      Returns:
      an iterator over the String elements of this queue in front-to-back order

    • equals

      boolean equals(QueueADT that)
      Compares this queue to the specified queue for equality.

      Two queues are considered equal if and only if they contain the same String elements appearing in the same order from front to back. Equality of individual elements is determined using String.equals(Object).

      Parameters:
      that - the QueueADT to compare to this queue; must not be null
      Returns:
      true if both queues contain equal elements in the same order; false otherwise

    • toArray

      String[] toArray(String[] holder) throws NullPointerException
      Copies all elements of this queue into the provided String array in proper sequence, from front to back. If the provided array is large enough, it is used directly; otherwise, a new array of the same type and sufficient size is allocated and returned.
      Parameters:
      holder - the String array into which the elements of this queue are to be stored; must not be null
      Returns:
      a String array containing all elements of this queue in front-to-back order
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if holder is null

    • size

      int size()
      Returns the number of elements currently in this queue.
      Returns:
      the current size of the queue; never negative
